body:
`@adlc/core`'s `fence()` derives its delimiter tag from the fenced content's own length, so whoever wrote that content can compute the closing marker and terminate the fence early. Everything after their forged marker reaches the model as instructions instead of data. Reproduced: see #1005.

ROOT CAUSE (packages/core/lib/text.mjs:47-50):

    const capped = tail(raw, maxChars);
    const tag = `${label}-${capped.length}`;
    return `<<UNTRUSTED:${marker}:${tag}>>\n${capped}\n<<END:${label}:${tag}>>`;

`label` is a literal at every call site and `capped.length` is exactly `maxChars` whenever content exceeds the cap, so the tag is fully determined by values the content author knows. Un-truncated content is forgeable too — the tag is then a fixed point on the attacker's own payload length, solvable by padding.

SCOPE OF EXPOSURE: 17 of 18 call sites. The only defended one is packages/autopilot/lib/triage.mjs:82, which already puts a per-call randomBytes(8) nonce in the LABEL after a codex review round found this same defect. That local fix is why 17 others still carry it — CONVENTIONS.md:35 directs authors to work around core rather than fix it.

WHAT TO BUILD

1. packages/core/lib/text.mjs — replace the length-derived tag with a per-call nonce from node:crypto randomUUID(). Unguessable by construction; transparent to every caller.
2. packages/core/test/text.test.mjs — add a hostile fixture asserting that content containing a predicted close marker CANNOT terminate the fence. Put it beside the 22 existing fence assertions. This is the red test: write it first and watch it fail against the current implementation.
3. scripts/test/prompt-fencing.test.mjs — close the completeness hole. Today GUARDED is three hand-written entries and the only completeness assertion is `GUARDED.length >= 3`, which is vacuous: a new prompt builder that never calls fence() keeps the suite green.
   Make the rule DECIDABLE, not heuristic. Define the candidate set mechanically as: every file under packages/*/lib/ and packages/*/bin/ that imports an LLM-calling helper from @adlc/core (the `complete`/provider surface — derive the exact export names by reading packages/core/lib/llm.mjs and its index re-exports). For each candidate assert it appears in EITHER `GUARDED` or a new `UNGUARDED_REVIEWED` array whose entries are `{ file, reason }`. A file in neither fails the test by name.
   This fails closed on any newly added prompt builder and forces a human to record a reason rather than silently skipping the guard. Do NOT attempt to detect 'embeds untrusted content' by parsing source text — that judgment is exactly what the allowlist records.
   Seed `UNGUARDED_REVIEWED` with whatever current candidates are genuinely not embedding externally-authored content, one line of reason each; do not add a file to it to make the test pass without stating why.
4. CONVENTIONS.md rule 2 — amend the core freeze to carve out defect fixes. Core is frozen to ADDITIONS; a defect in a core primitive is fixed in core, because working around it locally multiplies the divergence core exists to prevent. This ticket is the worked example.

TWO TESTS PIN THE VULNERABLE FORMAT and must be updated as part of the fix — this is not test-weakening, because each asserts an implementation detail that IS the defect, and the assertion's intent (content is fenced) survives:
  - packages/coldstart/test/coldstart.test.mjs:110 asserts the literal `:TICKET-8000>>`
  - packages/fleet/test/adapter-shared.test.mjs:45-46 assert `PRIOR_ATTEMPT_1-8`
Replace each with an assertion that does not depend on a predictable tag — prefer asserting the fence cannot be closed by its own content, which is strictly stronger than the literal it replaces.

DO NOT fix this by editing call sites. Every fence() caller is a declared rail on this ticket: the whole point is that one shared primitive is correct so 18 call sites need no per-package defence. autopilot's existing label nonce becomes redundant but harmless — leave it as defence in depth.

OUT OF SCOPE: tail()'s truncation direction (#1007). It is a real defect in the same function, but it changes behaviour at call sites and must be reviewable and revertable separately from a security fix.

ACCEPTANCE
- A hostile fixture proves forged content cannot close the fence; the test fails before the change and passes after.
- `npm test` green from the repo root, output shown.
- `node --test packages/core/test/` green.
- The completeness check fails by name when a candidate file is in neither GUARDED nor UNGUARDED_REVIEWED: verify by adding a throwaway probe in a SIBLING package (e.g. packages/spec-lint/lib/__probe.mjs) that imports a prompt sender from core, asserting the test goes red, then deleting it. NOT packages/core/lib/ — a file inside core imports './llm.mjs' relatively, which the from-core detector cannot see, so a probe placed there passes and verifies nothing. Corrected during build after the original probe silently succeeded.
- `adlc rails-guard --base origin/main --ticket <this ticket id>` exits 0, proving no call site was touched.
- `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs --max 80` on the diff.

SCOPE NOTE (added during build): the fix makes fence() non-deterministic, so every test asserting a literal tag or byte-identical prompts fails. Four more test files join scope for that reason: packages/autopilot/test/triage.test.mjs, packages/fleet/test/adapter-shared.test.mjs, packages/fleet/test/charters.test.mjs, packages/review-calibration/test/judge-bounding.test.mjs. One of them — adapter-shared.test.mjs:49 'fence tag is length-derived so forged inner END markers cannot predict it' — asserts the DEFECT as a security property. It passes only because its single fixture guesses a wrong length. Replace it with an assertion that the tag is unpredictable by construction, and record it as a hollow-test lesson.
title: Make fence() unforgeable and close the fencing completeness gap (#1005)
